expected_tradeoff: Targets U: +4 expected from tombstone-responsiveness re-scoping (ckpt_09/13/22/16 no_memory -> answer), +1 from the >=2 answer-bearing threshold (ckpt_04 answer_redacted -> answer); the agent top_k default 8->11 is a bounded swing at the remaining 5 sparse-logistics checkpoints. A and F both stay 0.0: no gate or release set widens (tombstone_terms feeds only denial classification, never allowed; the cap raise adds only already-cleared live records) and deleted content remains cryptographically gone. Residual risk is a small U dip if the cap raise admits chatty allowed rows that dilute the no-LLM join, mitigated by overlap-first ranking and reversible next iteration.
retrieval_loop: retrieve() PASS-1 keeps gate-0 responsiveness-first ordering but _is_responsive's tombstoned branch no longer returns _DEFAULT_OVERLAP unconditionally: when the record has captured rows in tombstone_terms it returns the count of distinct query digests present there (0 => not responsive => the tombstone is skipped, so an unrelated deletion cannot shadow live allowed content); when the record has no captured rows (legacy or term-free) it falls back to _DEFAULT_OVERLAP to preserve the conservative direction. PASS-2 gates, denied lists, access_log audit rows, and the top_k hard cap on allowed are unchanged. The answer-bearing classification increments query_answer_denials only when real content overlap (total minus structural) is >= 2, so a single incidental shared content token no longer downgrades a complete answer to answer_redacted.
forgetting_mechanism: tombstone() inserts the record's HMAC term digests into tombstone_terms in the same transaction, then purges record_terms, nulls key material, zeroes ciphertext and blanks plaintext bodies exactly as before, so an index never outlives the body in the clear. tombstone_terms stores only keyed digests (per-store HMAC key, truncated 16-hex, same as record_terms) and is read only to scope tombstone responsiveness for denial classification - never to resurrect content into allowed. A query that names the deleted fact's vocabulary still matches and forces no_memory; a disjoint-vocabulary query sees only cleared live records about other content, so deleted facts stay unreconstructable and F remains 0.
